speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; please describe the specific nature of your increasing right knee pain and swelling, and tell me more about the pain episodes you experience when urinating. Additionally, could you elaborate on your history of the painful, swollen left ankle joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The combination of urethritis (pain with urination), recent onset monoarthritis (knee, preceded by ankle), and a history of inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of this condition. I will confirm this diagnosis by checking for urethral discharge and inflammatory markers. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urethral Swab, and ESR/CRP.
